title: Integer expressions
description: Integer expressions denote sets of numbers; asking whether two of them denote different sets was among the first problems shown Sigma-2-complete (Stockmeyer and Meyer). The solutions are the numbers of expression 1 that expression 2 cannot make: the abstraction derives a number by choosing a side at every union, and the check tries to derive the same number from expression 2. Only the derived atom value/1 is glued and the loop is Shape 2, so the derivation is a hidden witness and each number is counted once.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The two expressions and their subexpressions. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% Integer expressions are built from numbers with plus(A,B) (add a number of A to a
% number of B) and union(A,B) (a number of A or a number of B); each denotes a set.
num(0..100).
% Expression 1: the amounts that four coins from {1, 5, 10, 25} can make.
expr(1, plus(plus(C,C),plus(C,C))) :- C = union(union(1,5),union(10,25)).
% Expression 2: the amounts that three coins from {2, 5, 10, 20} can make.
expr(2, plus(plus(C,C),C)) :- C = union(union(2,5),union(10,20)).
% at(P,E): the subexpression E sits at position P. Positions tell equal subexpressions
% apart: e(I) is the root of expression I, l(P) and r(P) are the two parts below P.
at(e(I),E) :- expr(I,E).
at(l(P),A) :- at(P,plus(A,_)).
at(r(P),B) :- at(P,plus(_,B)).
at(l(P),A) :- at(P,union(A,_)).
at(r(P),B) :- at(P,union(_,B)).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): numbers of expression 1, each with a derivation.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a number of expression 1. A derivation walks down from the root; it
% takes both parts of a plus and chooses one part of a union.
live(e(1)).
live(l(P)) :- live(P), at(P,plus(_,_)).
live(r(P)) :- live(P), at(P,plus(_,_)).
1 { live(l(P)); live(r(P)) } 1 :- live(P), at(P,union(_,_)).
% The number is the sum of the numbers it reaches.
value(S) :- S = #sum { K,P : live(P), at(P,K), num(K) }.
#show value/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atom: the number, not its derivation.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a derivation of the same number from expression 2 (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: expression 2 can make the same number.
walk(e(2)).
walk(l(P)) :- walk(P), at(P,plus(_,_)).
walk(r(P)) :- walk(P), at(P,plus(_,_)).
1 { walk(l(P)); walk(r(P)) } 1 :- walk(P), at(P,union(_,_)).
:- value(S), #sum { K,P : walk(P), at(P,K), num(K) } != S.
#show.
#show part(K,P) : walk(P), at(P,K), num(K).

% The counterexample depends on the number only: this number is not a solution.
relevant(value(S)) :- value(S).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

library.summary: Numbers that one integer expression denotes and another does not (Stockmeyer and Meyer); the candidate is a derived number, its derivation a hidden witness (22 solutions).
